name: com.subsola/subsola
title: Subsola
description: What public records say is under US city streets: utilities, depths, lead lines and digs.

tools.name: whats_under
tools.description: Looks up what public records say is under the street in front of one street address in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Dallas, and San Jose. Returns each utility likely in the street (water, sewer, storm drain, gas, electric, telecom, steam) with its distance from the lot line, its expected depth and the code or standard behind it, and how the line was placed (the owner's published map, excavation permits on the block, or inferred) with a confidence label; the water service line's lead status where the city publishes it by address; the house sewer; digging permitted there today; the newest permits out front, each with its street, its distance from the address and its issue date (or its start date, marked scheduled when the work hasn't begun), and whether it is one of several permits for the same long-running job; and the nearest hydrant, catch basin and manhole. Use it for site research, scoping an excavation, or due diligence on a property: what is under the street or sidewalk at an address, whether planned digging might meet a line, and whether the service line is lead. Answers are public-records evidence with a records-as-of date, not a survey or a utility locate, and end with the city's 811 notice. An address outside these cities, or with no exact match, returns an error saying what was found instead.

address.description: A street address with house number, in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Dallas, or San Jose. Include the city, e.g. "200 N Spring St, Los Angeles" or "33 Union Square West, Manhattan".

city.description: Which city the address is in, to search only that city and rule out a lookalike address elsewhere. One of "nyc" for New York City, "dc" for Washington, DC, "sf" for San Francisco, "la" for Los Angeles, "sd" for San Diego, "sea" for Seattle, "den" for Denver, "chi" for Chicago, "dal" for Dallas, "sj" for San Jose. The full name or a common short form works too, in any case: "Los Angeles", "NYC", "Brooklyn", "D.C.".

tools.name: recent_digs
tools.description: Lists utility excavation permits on the blocks around one street address in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Dallas, and San Jose, newest first, at most 25 with the total found: the utility, the permit holder, what the work was, the issue date (or, where a city publishes none, the start date) and work window, whether digging is permitted today or scheduled to start later, the street and its distance, and, for a job permitted again and again, how many permits it has run to since when. Use it to see who holds permits on a block, what work is open now or scheduled, which jobs drag on, and how often the street gets opened, when planning or coordinating work there. Narrow with radius_m, since_year, utility or permitted_today. Permits that don't cut the street (opening a manhole, storing material) are left out. Answers are public-records evidence with a records-as-of date and end with the city's 811 notice.

address.description: A street address with house number, in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Dallas, or San Jose. Include the city, e.g. "200 N Spring St, Los Angeles" or "33 Union Square West, Manhattan".

city.description: Which city the address is in, to search only that city and rule out a lookalike address elsewhere. One of "nyc" for New York City, "dc" for Washington, DC, "sf" for San Francisco, "la" for Los Angeles, "sd" for San Diego, "sea" for Seattle, "den" for Denver, "chi" for Chicago, "dal" for Dallas, "sj" for San Jose. The full name or a common short form works too, in any case: "Los Angeles", "NYC", "Brooklyn", "D.C.".

radius_m.description: How far around the address to look, in meters. Default 150, at most 400.

since_year.description: Only permits issued in this year or later. Where a city publishes no issue date (Los Angeles, Denver), the year the work starts counts.

utility.description: Only this kind of work: "electric" (electric), "gas" (gas), "telecom" (telecom), "water" (water), "sewer" (sewer), "steam" (steam), "capital" (city rebuild).

permitted_today.description: true for only the permits whose work window includes today.
